principles: understand the information relationship before composing the page
use the title to state a conclusion or judgment whenever evidence supports one
establish a clear hierarchy and one dominant visual anchor
allocate visual weight intentionally instead of distributing it evenly
use whitespace as an information-organization tool
prefer alignment and spatial relationships over container proliferation
keep one design language across a deck while varying composition by meaning
alternate dense, quiet, transition and peak pages to create deck rhythm
make every decorative element serve information or remove it
solve high density with editing, grid and hierarchy before shrinking type
preserve content truth, immutable facts and source provenance
make key text, numbers, charts and structural shapes natively editable
